title_en: Alginate-derived smart hydrogel dressing with CaP/ZnO synergy for on-demand hemostasis and pH-triggered curcumin delivery
title_zh: Alginate-derived smart hydrogel dressing with CaP/ZnO synergy for on-demand hemostasis and pH-triggered curcumin delivery
authors: Kamrun Nahar Fatema, Md Rokon Ud Dowla Biswas, Longlong Li, Biswajit Mahanty, Khurshid Ahmad, Ishrat Jahan, Sungtae Yang, Jongyun Kim, Dong-Weon Lee
journal: Journal of Drug Delivery Science and Technology
notes: Published online: 2026-06-30. ISSN: 1773-2247. Abstract: Effective wound management requires dressings that provide both rapid hemostasis and active healing. We developed a multifunctional hydrogel wound dressing CSPCZ (CMC/SA/PAA cross-linked with CaP/ZnO) integrating sodium alginate (SA), carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), and poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) with calcium phosphate (CaP) and zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles. Curcumin (Cur), selected for its potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties, was incorporated to address infection and oxidative stress. The hydrogel exhibited high porosity (85%), optimal moisture vapor transmission (~1511 g m-2 day-1), strong antioxidant activity, and excellent biocompatibility (>95% cell viability). It exhibited three synergistic pH-responsive functions: under mildly acidic conditions, partial CaP dissolution may reinforce Ca-alginate crosslinking, resulting in a compact network and slower Cur release; under neutral-to-alkaline conditions, increased swelling promotes accelerated Cur release (~18% at pH 5.4, 65% at pH 7.4, and 90% at pH 8.4 over 5 days); and cation-mediated coagulation enables rapid hemostasis, reducing bleeding time from 180 +/- 5 s to 100 +/- 5 s in vivo. By integrating rapid hemostasis with intelligent, pH-triggered drug release, the CSPCZ platform addresses critical gaps in current wound management. These integrated properties establish the CSPCZ hydrogel as a multifunctional, pH-responsive platform for rapid hemostasis and controlled curcumin delivery. Keywords: Curcumin; Hemostasis; pH-responsive release.
